claims.claim: Promotion moves only the block: a pair takes the topmost slot among itself and the sharing singles above it, singles fill the rest in order, rows outside the block keep their positions.
claims.excerpt:
"""One promotion: the topmost pair that has a sharing single above it takes
    the topmost slot of its block. Only block members change position."""
    for j, pair in enumerate(rows):
        if not pair.is_pair:
            continue
        above = [i for i in range(j) if not rows[i].is_pair and (rows[i].variants & pair.variants)]
        if not above:
            continue
        slots = above + [j]
        movers = [rows[i] for i in above]
        promoted = replace(
            pair,
            promoted_over=pair.promoted_over + tuple(
                v for r in movers for v in sorted(r.variants, key=_variant_key)),
        )
        out = list(rows)
        out[slots[0]] = promoted
        for slot, mover in zip(slots[1:], movers):
            out[slot] = mover
        return out, True
    return rows, False

claims.excerpt: verify_rule.py R1 coverage gap: it enumerates permutations only for n in (2,3) while the gate accepts up to 10 rows (docs/22 Step 6) and the ladder has 10 rungs. At n=4 the same rule lowers the score in 5,220 of 327,600 comparisons. Mechanism: promote_allele_sharing inserts the pair at the single's position, shifting every row between them down one rank; at n<=3 a shift cannot cross a tier boundary (ranks 2,3 share the 50-point tier), at n>=4 it can (rank 3->4 crosses 50->25). First counterexample (reproduced verbatim): orig = [single chr1:1000, single chr1:2000, single chr2:3000, pair chr1:1000+chr1:2000], truth = (chr2:3000, chr2:4000): original scores 25.0 (partial at rank 3), ruled scores 12.5 (partial pushed to rank 4 by the insertion shift, though the pair shares no allele with it).

review 741aaad logic error 4:
R2 overgeneralization: 'keeping the weaker one below never scored lower than dropping it' was measured only on 2-row files (ranks 1,2). With bystander rows it fails: keep = [pair chr1:1000+chr2:3000, single chr3:5000, single chr2:4000, pair chr1:1000+chr1:2000] scores 25.0 under truth (chr1:1000, chr1:2000) while dropping the last row scores 50.0. This is the document's own headline phenomenon (full match at rank 4 = 25 < partial at rank 1 = 50) re-entering through the 'both are kept' mandate for allele-sharing pairs; the R2 verification design cannot see it. The keep-policy may still be the right tradeoff under ignorance, but the stated measurement support is an unproven universal.
